html: Seasonal allergies happen when the immune system reacts to airborne substances such as tree, grass or weed pollen. Symptoms often come and go with the seasons.

image.alt: Illustration of pollen grains drifting from a flowering plant
image.caption: Pollen counts tend to be highest on warm, dry, windy days.
image.title: Illustration of pollen grains drifting from a flowering plant

html:
• Sneezing and a runny or stuffy nose
  • Itchy, watery eyes
  • Itchy throat or ears
  • Tiredness from poor sleep

• Check local pollen forecasts and limit time outdoors on high-count days
  • Keep windows closed during peak season
  • Shower and change clothes after spending time outside
  • Ask a pharmacist about over-the-counter options
Talk with a health care professional if symptoms interfere with sleep or daily activities, last for months, or come with wheezing or shortness of breath.
